annotations.title: Lest they should be conuerted.
annotations.text: [1] These speaches here and els where, we must not so vnderstand as though he spake in parables of purpose and to this end, that the hearers might not vnderstand, lest they should be conuerted: which were as much to say as that he would not haue them vnderstand, nor be conuerted: but we must learne the true sense of this very place in S. Matthew [2] and in the Actes, [3]where our Sauiour and S. Paul speake thus, They haue heard heauily, and haue shut their eies, lest perhaps they may see, and vnderstand, and be conuerted, and I heale them. Whereby it is euident, that the speaking in parables was not the cause (for many beside the Apostles heard and vnderstood) but them selues would not heare, and vnderstand, and be conuerted: and so were the cause of their owne wilful and obstinate infidelity. And therfore also he spake in parables, because they were not worthy to vnderstand, as the other to whom he expounded them.

notes.text: God is not author of sinne, but mans owne will.

annotations.title: And sleepe.
annotations.text: The Church, and Christs doctrine, (sleepe we, wake we) increaseth by the great prouidence of God. only the preachers must sow, and plant, and water, and <mn>◦</mn> God wil giue the increase, nourishing the seede in mens harts. And therfore we may not giue ouer, or be impatient and solicitous, if we haue not alwaies good successe: but doing our duty, commit the rest to God.

annotations.title: Mustard seed.
annotations.text: ◦ If the Church and Truth had more and more decaied and been obscured after the Apostles time vnto ours, as the Heretikes hold: then had it been great in the beginning, and smal afterward: where this Parable saith contrary, that it was a mustard seed first, and afterward a great tree. vide Chrys. to. 5 contra Gentiles in vita S. Babylæ Mart.

annotations.title: The birdes.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Of al sectes or doctrine, Christs religion at the beginning was the smallest, and most contemptible: but the successe thereof farre passed al mans doctrine: in so much that afterward al the wisest and greatest of the world made their residence and rest therein.
